text:
Dallas is 10-6-2 with 22 points, a good team doing about what its chances say (20.7 expected points). The Stars hold 52.4% of the expected goals and allow only 2.8 per 60 minutes. Our playoff race likes them at 77%.

The story around the team keeps circling Jason Robertson. His contract and trade rumors haven't gone away, and the insider talk this week only added to it. On the ice he keeps answering: a hat trick in 5:20 earlier this month, the third-fastest in franchise history, and a power-play goal last Saturday. Mikko Rantanen ran a three-game goal streak, and his line with Wyatt Johnston and Sam Steel controls 62% of the expected goals.

The concerns are on the back end. Miro Heiskanen has missed games with an upper-body injury, which pushes Thomas Harley and Nils Lundkvist to carry the top minutes (56% of expected goals, fine but not Heiskanen). The second pair of Tyler Myers and Lian Bichsel sits at 42%. Dallas also takes more penalties than it draws (4.06 a game against 3.11).

Then there's Jake Oettinger. He's .842 over his last five starts, 4.3 goals worse than expected, and Thursday's 8-3 loss in Winnipeg was ugly. Oettinger's track record says this is a slump, not who he is. Watch for Heiskanen's return and whether Oettinger's save percentage climbs with him.
headline: The Stars are solid, but the net is shaky
